pages.text: A tank block stores $(l)32,000 mB$() (32 buckets) of a single fluid:

$(li)the $(l)Liquid Tank$() (a steel line around the glass, waves on its lid) takes liquids: water, lava, Coolant, Cryo Coolant, Acid, liquids of other mods;$(br)$(li)the $(l)Gas Tank$() (a mint line around the glass, a cloud on its lid) takes gases: biogas, methane, Steam, gases of other mods.

$(l)Tanks grow.$() Blocks of the same kind that fill a box, of any size up to 16 on a side, join into one tank: a column, a row, a 2x2x2, a 3x3x3. Each block adds 32 buckets, and pipes and buckets see them as one. Tanks already holding different fluids don't join.

Fill them with the matching $(l:cables/cables)pipe$(/l): a $(l:cables/liquid_pipe)Liquid Pipe$(/l) or a $(l:cables/gas_pipe)Gas Pipe$(/l), on any free face of any block, top and bottom too: a collar, steel on the Liquid Tank and mint on the Gas Tank, shows where one plugs in. A Liquid Tank also takes and gives $(l)buckets$(): just right-click it with one.$(br2)Tanks are $(l)passive$(): they never push

anything out. To empty one into a machine, right-click the arm of the pipe that touches it, so the pipe $(l)pulls$() from the tank (an orange collar shows it). A joined tank has one frame around its outside and one pane of glass on each side, however many blocks it has. Through it you see into the tank, right through to the other side, and the

fluid inside stands up to its level with its own colour (gases look hazy); shift + right-click a tank, with anything in hand, to read the exact amount.$(br2)$(l)Look at a tank$() to see a panel over it with what is inside and how full it is, one panel for a whole joined tank.
A tank is a handy buffer: put one between a Methane Extractor and the Gas Turbines, or between a Water Pump and a Fission Reactor, and it keeps the flow going when production dips.
Breaking a block $(l)loses what that block held$(); the rest stays in the other blocks, which join up again where they can.
